review.material: Annual Edition 2025 local PDF: preface; §§3.1–3.2 selected triangle and group definitions; §5.2 opening; §14.1 action, orbit and equivalence discussion read.
review.limitations: Later quotient, representation, ring and field arguments and most exercises were not reviewed. This guide covers selected group-theory entry points, not the entire book.

sections.title: What this book is about
sections.text: A broad undergraduate algebra text combining proof, worked examples and applications. The selected route begins with rigid motions of a triangle, abstracts their shared laws into a group, then studies polygon symmetries and actions on sets.

sections.title: The essential structure
sections.text: A group consists of a set and an associative binary operation with an identity and inverses. Commutativity is extra, not required. Composing two triangle motions in reverse orders can produce different results, showing why the operation must be specified.

sections.title: How the explanation develops
sections.text: Concrete symmetry permutations motivate a multiplication table before the axioms are stated. For a regular n-gon, choosing the first vertex image and one of two neighboring images for the second counts 2n motions. Rotation and reflection generate the resulting group.

sections.title: Actions turn algebra into motion
sections.text: A left action obeys ex=x and (gh)x=g(hx). Objects connected by some group element are equivalent; their equivalence classes are orbits. This separates a group element from the particular point or configuration on which it acts.

sections.title: Notation worth checking
sections.text: Judson writes D_n for the n-gon symmetry group of order 2n; other authors use different subscripts. Function composition applies the rightmost map first. Retain these conventions when comparing the book with the square explorer.

sections.title: A useful reading task
sections.text: Reproduce two triangle compositions and see whether they commute. Then identify the group, acted-on set and orbit for one square example. A list of visually similar drawings alone does not specify a group action.

terms.meaning: A compatible rule for a group to transform a set.
All images of one object under an action.
